newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania says meningitis virus still unidentified.
newsitem.headline: Romania says meningitis virus still unidentified.

text.p: Experts at France's Pasteur Institute have failed to identify the specific virus which killed 38 people in Romania's worst viral meningitis epidemic in a decade, Romanian health authorities said on Wednesday.
"So far the Pasteur Institute in Paris could not identify the pathogen agent behind the meningitis epidemic in Romania," the health ministry said in a statement.

Romania sought help from Western medical experts after local institutes failed to identify the virus which triggered the epidemic which has spread to nearly half the Balkan country, with most cases registered in its capital Bucharest.
Romania would also send test samples for identification to Britain's Collindale Institute, the statement said.
As many as 444 patients, including some 50 children, were hospitalised across Romania after the epidemic began at the end of July. Of the 38 death toll, most were elderly people.
The viral disease, which usually lasts a week, causes high fever, headaches and vomiting and affects the gastro-intestinal tract.

Tourists returning from Cyprus apparently brought the disease to Romania, medical experts said. More than 100 people fell ill with mild meningitis in Limassol, the southern coastal hub of Cyprus's tourist industry, in July.
In 1986 Romania suffered an epidemic of the more dangerous bacterial meningitis which killed some 15,000 people in central Africa this year.
